attempts.prompt:
Use case: compositing. Image1 is the sole authority for clothing, pose, hair, expression, light, and crop. Image2 provides only the mascot identity and anatomy. Transform the human anatomy into a smooth golden-yellow compact near-round mascot head and body, featuring green-ringed black eyes and a mouth matching the source expression. Preserve the actual source features: a bare head with short, thick dark black/brown hair brushed back with a side part and wave, natural brows, and an understated smooth upper lip and chin with no prominent separate moustache or beard. No spectacles. Maintain the serious closed mouth and the dark navy open suit lapels over a white/pale shirt and dark necktie with limited pale diagonal/block pattern. Ensure the rounded chin immediately meets the raised and broadened existing neckline, creating a very short, broad neck transition with minimal throat exposure. Avoid any separate yellow neck shaft, pointed V funnel, pinched collar, neck rolls, floating collar, clipping, or cream belly bib. Preserve the actual open garment and fastening with coherent front/rear collar overlap and contact shadow. Retain the complete tilted dark frame and opaque photographic backing in its actual source color. An attached cream note is present in the source; preserve its original marks and overlap exactly. All solid surfaces must be opaque, with alpha only outside the complete card silhouette. No invented insignia, text, or accessories. Fine primary details that are indistinct in the source must remain understated.
FINAL EXACT SOURCE REQUIREMENT: BAREHEADED strong IMAGE-LEFT near-profile/three-quarter civilian bust, short thick DARK BLACK/BROWN hair brushed back with side part/wave, actual brow HAIR and understated smooth upper lip/chin with no prominent separate moustache or beard, no spectacles. Serious CLOSED mouth. DARK NAVY OPEN suit lapels over WHITE/PALE shirt and DARK necktie with limited PALE diagonal/block pattern visible beside note. Keep actual primary head angle/roll and shadow, no military khaki uniform, shoulder straps, invented facial hair or cap. Fine upper-lip detail stays understated.
Retain exact primary head angle, expression, cap shape, real hair and visible clothing/decoration areas. One compact near-round yellow mascot head with a clearly ROUNDED short chin immediately contacting raised broad collar, no V-shaped lower-face funnel or yellow shaft. Preserve green-ringed black mascot eyes and real eyebrow HAIR. Do not copy human long neck or angular jaw into mascot anatomy; fit original neckline around compact round head. Preserve actual dark solid cloth and photographic backing opacity. Tiny ambiguous features remain understated; no new badge engraving or decoration outside actually exposed source regions. Preserve an attached note ONLY where actually present; otherwise do not invent one. Image1 exact original card; Image2 mascot identity/anatomy only.
Output alpha: genuine transparent RGBA ONLY OUTSIDE the complete original framed portrait silhouette. The photographic BACKING INSIDE the frame is a required OPAQUE surface: preserve its original background color and texture behind the character all the way to the inner frame rim. Never turn the gaps between frame and character into transparent holes or a window. Keep the actual frame angle and rim. Preserve an overlapping paper note, pin or other attachment ONLY when actually visible in this exact source; otherwise do not invent one. Do not invent a new backdrop outside the whole card. Retain source clothing, hair, headgear, lighting and crop at full generated resolution. All originally OPAQUE subject surfaces must remain FULLY OPAQUE (alpha 255): yellow head/body, hair, beard, dark or black clothing, coat lapels, collar, tie, buttons and decorations. Dark cloth is colored material, not transparent background. Never fade garment interiors into semi-transparent patches, holes, white haze or see-through fabric. Keep any genuine source outer-edge alpha falloff only at that actual exterior boundary; preserve actual source transparency rather than making the subject itself translucent.
